bills.title: Arizona High-Risk AI Assessment and Transparency Requirements
bills.summary: Would establish comprehensive risk assessment, transparency, and bias mitigation requirements for high risk AI systems, including evaluating the potential for discrimination or bias.

bills.title: California AI Content Provenance Disclosure
bills.summary: Would mandate that content generated by AI includes latent disclosures of data provenance that is "permanent or extraordinarily difficult to remove."

bills.title: Connecticut AI Regulatory Sandbox and Chatbot Safety for Minors
bills.summary: Would direct a state agency to develop a plan for a sandbox that tests innovative AI products and services under reduced regulatory requirements. Also requires companion chatbot platforms to implement safeguards for minors and include regular disclosures of the chatbot's non-human status.

bills.title: Georgia Generative AI Product Liability for Minors
bills.summary: Would classify generative AI systems as personal property for product liability cases involving minors, establishes liability for product sellers, and imposes a duty to warn of risks.

bills.title: Illinois Generative AI Developer and Deployer Accountability

bills.title: Illinois Chatbot Provider Liability for Harmful Information
bills.summary: Would provide that chatbot deployers may not disclaim liability if the chatbot provides materially misleading or harmful information that results in financial loss or other demonstrable harm.

bills.title: Illinois Chatbot Strict Product Liability
bills.summary: Would designate chatbots as products subject to strict liability, making providers legally responsible for user injuries regardless of care or direct relationship.

bills.title: Illinois AI Companion Chatbot Safety and Suicide Prevention
bills.summary: Would require AI companion operators to implement protocols for detecting and addressing suicidal ideation and to provide clear user notifications of the system's non-human status.

bills.title: Illinois Advanced AI Developer Liability Safe Harbor
bills.summary: Would provide liability protections for developers of advanced AI models, contingent on the publication of safety protocols and transparency reports.

bills.title: Maryland Comprehensive Chatbot Privacy and Safety Regulation
bills.summary: Would set comprehensive regulations for the design, deployment, and operation of chatbots, including setting consumer privacy protections. Would prohibit operators from using chat logs for targeted advertising, profiling users beyond what is necessary to respond to prompts, and retaining chat logs for more than ten years. Developers and operators would be required to implement robust data security programs, conduct monthly safety testing, and publicly disclose their findings.

Also provides immunity to AI developers from liability for damages arising from the misuse of their systems by third parties, except when the developer should have known the system would be used for illegal purposes.

bills.title: Alabama Online Platform Age Verification
bills.summary: The House concurred to the Senate's amendment and passed the bill on February 10, 2026. The Senate amendment added language providing that compliance with the bill's proposed age verification requirements does not relieve an entity's age verification requirements under any other laws. The bill has now moved on to Governor Ivey for action.
bills.status_detail: Passed both chambers on February 10, 2026; sent to Governor Ivey

bills.title: Connecticut Genetic Information Privacy Act
bills.summary: Introduced by the Joint Committee on General Law in response to the CT Attorney General's urging for a standalone genetic data privacy law. Would apply to companies offering genetic testing directly to consumers.

bills.title: Georgia Online Safety and Privacy Protections for Consumers and Minors
bills.summary: Bipartisan AADC-style bill proposing robust online privacy and safety protections for both consumers and minors, similar to protections established in Nebraska, Vermont, and South Carolina. Would prohibit covered entities from engaging in high-risk data practices or design features unless the consumer explicitly requests the practice and the entity has implemented age assurance. Requires risk assessments for compulsive use in minors, default settings protections, algorithmic feed controls for minors, and prominent disclosures. Creates a private right of action in addition to Attorney General enforcement.

bills.title: Georgia App Store Accountability Act Age Assurance Framework
bills.summary: App Store Accountability Act-style age assurance framework with requirements for age verifying existing accounts, parental consent obligations for pre-installed apps, and no application exemptions.

bills.title: Illinois Minnesota-Style Comprehensive Privacy with Data Broker Delete Act
bills.summary: Minnesota-style comprehensive privacy bill that also includes a Delete Act requiring data brokers to register with the state annually and the state to establish an accessible deletion mechanism allowing consumers to submit one deletion request to all registered data brokers.

bills.title: Maryland MODPA Amendments on Geolocation, Immigration Enforcement, and Sensitive Data
bills.summary: Broad MODPA amendment that would expand the definition of precise geolocation data, narrow the definition of publicly available information, re-name sensitive data as sensitive attribute, narrow the DPPA data-level exemption, prohibit controllers from selling personal data for immigration enforcement purposes, and narrow the exception for compliance with civil, criminal, or regulatory inquiries to exclude immigration enforcement.

bills.title: Maryland MODPA Extension to Fully Autonomous Vehicles
bills.summary: Would amend MODPA to apply to any person that collects personal data through the use or operation of a fully autonomous vehicle (level 4 or 5 system). Also adds a new subtitle to the Transportation Article regulating fully autonomous vehicles.

bills.title: Maryland Data Broker Registration and Security Program
bills.summary: Would require data brokers to register with the state annually and to maintain a comprehensive information security program.

bills.title: Maryland Data Broker Registration and Security Program (House Companion)
bills.summary: House companion to SB 616. Would require data brokers to register with the state annually and to maintain a comprehensive information security program.

bills.title: Maryland Data Broker Registration
bills.summary: Data broker bill similar to SB 616 but less detailed, including failure to define direct relationship.

bills.title: Maine Maryland-Style Comprehensive Privacy with Data Minimization
bills.summary: Broad, Maryland-style comprehensive privacy bill with substantive data minimization requirements. Carried over from the 2025 legislative session. Passed the Maine House on February 10, 2026.

bills.title: New Jersey AADC-Style Amendments to Comprehensive Privacy Law for Minors
bills.summary: Would amend New Jersey's comprehensive privacy law to incorporate AADC-style requirements similar to Nebraska and Vermont, and includes third-party audit requirements similar to South Carolina that covered online services would be required to publicly and prominently post on the service's website.

bills.title: New Jersey AADC-Style Amendments to Comprehensive Privacy Law for Minors (Assembly Companion)
bills.summary: Assembly companion to S3413. Would amend New Jersey's comprehensive privacy law to incorporate AADC-style requirements similar to Nebraska and Vermont, and includes third-party audit requirements that covered online services would be required to publicly post.

bills.title: Rhode Island Age-Appropriate Design Code
bills.summary: AADC-style bill that includes a CPA/CTDPA-style duty of care and requires covered entities to conduct DPIAs, restrict certain processing activities, and implement high-level default privacy settings for known minors.

bills.title: Virginia Social Graph Data, AI Model Operator Context, and Social Media Interoperability
bills.summary: The Virginia Senate voted 40-0 to pass this bill concerning social graph data processed by a social media platform, contextual data processed by an artificial intelligence model operator, and interoperability requirements for social media. The Senate amended the bill, adjusting the definition of artificial intelligence and adding a definition of operator.

bills.title: Wisconsin Vermont-Style Age-Appropriate Design Code
bills.summary: Vermont-style AADC bill introduced on February 6, 2026.
